newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU mortgage rates may fall further - federation.
newsitem.headline: EU mortgage rates may fall further - federation.

text.p: European mortgage rates may fall further in some EU countries, including France, Germany and Austria, despite having already reached historical lows, the European Mortgage Federation said on Thursday.
"More tentative falls in rates are to be seen in France, Denmark and Norway," the federation said in a statement.
It also forecast a decline in German and Austrian mortgage rates, "probably followed by a slight rise if there is improvement in the economic climate".

The federation's statistics for the fourth quarter of 1996 show that rates fell again in Germany by 0.4 percentage point, Belgium (0.7 point), the Netherlands (0.6 point), Italy (1.2 points) and Sweden (0.8 point).

European mortgage rates currently stand at an average of about eight percent, down from almost 14 percent in 1992. Luxembourg offers the cheaper housing credit with a rate of 5.5 percent in the last quarter of 1996, whereas Greece had the most expensive rate of 16.8 percent.
Mortgage rates rose slightly in Britain and Ireland in the same period, reflecting money market trends, the federation said.
